name: Question 20
worked_solution:
We note that $b=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined.

The equation has the denominators $36b$ and $12{b}^{2}.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(36b,12{b}^{2})=36{b}^{2}.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $36{b}^{2},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5b+8}{12{b}^{2}} & =-\frac{12}{36b}+\frac{4b+8}{12{b}^{2}} \\ 36{b}^{2}\cdot (\frac{5b+8}{12{b}^{2}}) & =36{b}^{2}\cdot (-\frac{12}{36b}+\frac{4b+8}{12{b}^{2}}) \\ 36{b}^{2}\cdot (\frac{5b+8}{12{b}^{2}}) & =36{b}^{2}\cdot (-\frac{12}{36b})+36{b}^{2}\cdot (\frac{4b+8}{12{b}^{2}}) \\ 3\cdot 12{b}^{2}\cdot (\frac{5b+8}{12{b}^{2}}) & =b\cdot 36b\cdot (-\frac{12}{36b})+3\cdot 12{b}^{2}\cdot (\frac{4b+8}{12{b}^{2}}) \\ 3\cdot \cancel{12{b}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{5b+8}{\cancel{12{b}^{2}}}) & =b\cdot \cancel{36b}\cdot (-\frac{12}{\cancel{36b}})+3\cdot \cancel{12{b}^{2}}\cdot (\frac{4b+8}{\cancel{12{b}^{2}}}) \\ 3(5b+8) & =-12b+3(4b+8)\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $b,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}3(5b+8) & =-12b+3(4b+8) \\ 15b+24 & =-12b+12b+24 \\ 15b+24 & =24 \\ 15b & =24-24 \\ 15b & =0 \\ b & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $b=0$ as a solution. Since $b=0,$ we conclude that there is no solution.
